3.7.1.1.1  Advertised Price for Travel Services 

When it comes to advertising, Quebec legislation promotes full disclosure to enable the customer to make informed decisions, namely to ensure that pricing information is not misleading and that the total price is provided at the actual time of purchase to avoid so-called "sticker shock." However, travel agents may exclude from the total cost of the services advertised the Quebec sales tax, Canada’s goods and services tax and the 

dollar amount payable as a contribution to the compensation fund. The Travel Agent Act and its Regulation provide that a travel agent who wishes to unilaterally change the price of the travel services provided in a contract entered into with a client must insert a clause to that effect in the contract. The clause shall state that (i) the price may only be increased following the imposition of a fuel surcharge by the carrier or an increase in the exchange rate, insofar as the exchange rate applicable 45 days prior to the date on which the services are to be provided (the date of departure in most cases) has increased by more than 5% since the date on which the contract was entered into (the date of purchase in most cases); (ii) no price increase may occur within 30 days prior to the date on which the services are to be provided (once again, the date of departure in most cases); and (iii) if such price increase is equal to or greater than 7% of the price of the travel services, excluding the Quebec 

sales tax or Canada’s goods and services tax, the customer may choose between a full and immediate refund or 

the provision of similar services. 

Since January 1, 2017, Ontario’s legislation requires that any advertising indicating a trip’s price must also 

include all fees and taxes. The Travel Industry Act, 2002 requires any representation relating to the price of travel services to show in a clear, comprehensible and prominent manner the total amount consumers will be required to pay for the travel services, including all fees, levies, service charges, surcharges, taxes and other costs. All-inclusive prices reduce confusion and ensure that there are no surprises for consumers who purchase travel services in the province. 

While Ontario’s legislation also allows for price increases, it only allows them if the contract between the travel 

agent and the customer permits them, if the customer has not paid the price of the travel services in full, and if the cumulative price increase is less than 7% of the total price of the travel services, excluding any increase resulting from an increase in retail sales tax or federal goods and services tax. Otherwise, the travel agent must offer the customer the choice between a full and immediate refund of the amount paid and comparable alternate travel services acceptable to the customer. 3.7.2.1  International Regulatory Framework 

Numerous commercial aspects of international air transport are regulated by international conventions, principally the Convention on International Civil Aviation signed in Chicago on December 7, 1944 (the “ Chicago Transat A.T. Inc. – 2023 Annual Information Form page 28 

Convention ”), by the domestic legislation of countries in which air transport is conducted, and by a network of 

bilateral and multilateral air transport agreements and treaties. 

The Chicago Convention provides the basis for regulation of international air carrier operations. Scheduled air services are governed by the bilateral air transport agreements in effect between the countries of origin, destination and, in certain cases, transit of the flights in question. Certain principles pertaining to the operation of international charter flights were established between each of the signatory states (including Canada), namely that the intended transportation comply with, and be duly approved pursuant to, the national regulations of the countries between which it is being conducted. 

The Chicago Convention also established the International Civil Aviation Organization (the “ICAO”), a specialized 

agency of the United Nations whose purpose is to foster the planning and development of international air transport. Under the auspices of the ICAO, rules establishing minimum operational standards are normally agreed upon on a multilateral basis. One of the treaties with considerable consequence for Transat is the landmark air transport agreement concluded between Canada and the European Union (“EU”) in November 

2008. It formally entered into force on December 16, 2009. The agreement sets the rules for air transport services between Canada and the 27 member states of the EU and will liberalize market access in this respect on a progressive, phased-in basis. During the first phase, Canadian airlines are able to operate from any point in Canada to any point in the 27 member-state EU zone without restrictions, with EU-licensed air carriers enjoying reciprocal rights from any point in the EU (regardless of nationality) to any point in Canada. Subsequent liberalization phases will be contingent on the relaxation of Canadian airline ownership and control rules by foreign interest and will involve the easing of access to third-country markets. 

On November 5, 2003, the Montreal Convention of 1999 on Compensation for Accident Victims (the “ Montreal Convention ”) came into effect. This multilateral agreement updates the rules on passengers, baggage and cargo 

liability applicable to international air transport and originally established by the Warsaw Convention in 1929 

and amended over the years (together the “ Warsaw System ”). The Montreal Convention provides for the review of liability limits, thus ensuring that the amounts remain relevant with the passage of time. The first such review was duly undertaken by the ICAO during the course of 2009. In addition to establishing new principles of liability, the Montreal Convention modernizes many of the ticketing and air waybill requirements. The Montreal Convention has been ratified by Canada and applies to all flights between Canada and other ratifying states. For flights from Canada to non-ratifying or non-signatory states, the Warsaw System continues to govern. 

As an airline operating flights from airports within the EU, Air Transat is subject to the provisions of EU Regulation 261/2004. This directive establishes a legal framework for the compensation and care of passengers by airlines in the event of overbooking/denied boarding, flight cancellations and long delays. While the Regulation stipulates payable compensation in the event of the first two cases, it only expressly provides for a duty of care by the airline in the context of a long flight delay (meals, snacks, hotel accommodations, as applicable). In November 2009, the European Court of Justice issued a ruling that extended financial compensation obligations to long delays as well. This jurisprudential trend has been maintained and EU national enforcement bodies henceforth consider passengers on flights delayed by more than three hours as being eligible for compensation per the rates set out for overbooking/cancellation, except in certain narrowly defined cases of extraordinary circumstances. It should be noted that this regulation was introduced into British domestic law despite it leaving the EU. Transat A.T. Inc. – 2023 Annual Information Form page 29

Transat is committed to deploying its operations in a sustainable way and focuses on actions that have a positive impact on all of its stakeholders. The day-to-day management of risks and opportunities relating to 

environmental, social and governance (“ESG”) issue s is provided by Transat's Corporate Responsibility Department ("CR"). Since 2022, this department has been led by the Vice-President of Corporate Responsibility who reports directly to the Chief People, Sustainability and Communications Officer who is also an executive officer. 

During 2023, Transat adopted a 2024-2026 Corporate Responsibility Plan, which is based on three main pillars: people, planet and sustainable practices. An overview of our environmental protection, social engagement and good governance (ESG) strategy and performance is presented in our 2022-2023 Corporate Responsibility Report. This report, which covers the period from November 1, 2021, to October 31, 2023, was prepared based on the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TFCFD) to guide the discourse related to our overall approach on sustainability and how we address each issue. Transat's climate governance, strategy, risks and performance are also outlined in its report based on the recommendations of the TFCFD released in May 2023. Transat A.T. Inc. – 2023 Annual Information Form page 34 

3.8.1  People 

Transat is committed to maximizing the development and well-being of its employees and to fostering a caring, safe and inclusive work environment. This vision percolates down to our customers to whom we aspire to offer the safest and most accessible experience. 

Aviation safety and occupational health and safety 

The safety of our customers, staff and partners takes precedence in everything we do. At all times, we are committed to enforcing the highest industry standards for aviation safety, which means absolute compliance with current regulations. In December 2023, Air Transat once again successfully renewed its IOSA certification. IOSA certification is renewed every two years and demonstrates our commitment to the industry's highest standards of quality and safety. For more information, please see section 3.1.2 (Maintenance, Inspections, Safety and Other Measures). 

Diversity, equity, inclusion and accessibility 

We believe our success depends on the diversity of our staff, a true reflection of our customers, our partners and the communities where we operate. To support our ambition, we have begun a process of formalizing and communicating our DEI commitments to all our teams in 2023. Transat also deployed a self-identification survey to all its employees, in order to be better equipped to assess the Corporation's diversity profile, intensify its inclusion initiatives and define its objectives and targets. Awareness workshops and DEI training were also implemented. 

Transat recognizes the fundamental right of every passenger to be treated with dignity and respect. We are committed to honoring our obligations to identify, prevent and eliminate barriers for people living with disabilities, for both our customers and our employees. In accordance with the Accessible Canada Act , Transat, through its subsidiary Air Transat, has developed its first accessibility plan which is intended to evolve and will be implemented from 2023 to 2025. 

3.8.2  Planet 

Transat is committed to minimizing the negative environmental impacts of its business, thanks to a strategy focusing on the fight against climate change. Transat has several processes in place to ensure that it complies with the provisions of environmental laws and regulations applicable to its operations. The day-to-day management of environmental and climate risks, including a follow-up of the environmental management system, is provided by Transat's RE Department, a team dedicated to sustainable development and ESG. We are therefore able to develop plans to mitigate our environmental impacts and respect our environmental compliance obligations. 

Climate Action Plan 

To guide our actions, we have developed an ambitious decarbonization plan that aims to eliminate net carbon 

emissions by 2050. We have identified a target to reduce our net emissions of CO₂ per revenue tonne -kilometre (RTK) by 24% by 2030, compared to 2019. In order to achieve net zero emissions by 2050, we will need to use all commercial and economic levers currently available, including fleet renewal, sustainable aviation fuel 

(“SAF”), operational efficiency and purchase of carbon credits to offset residual emissions. Transat's climate Transat A.T. Inc. – 2023 Annual Information Form page 35 

plan involves certain assumptions and certain elements beyond its control; it will evolve depending on the availability of next generation aircraft, the availability of SAF, and government policies. 

The renewal of our fleet continues. In 2020, Air Transat retired the last aircraft in its former Airbus A310 fleet. These aircraft were replaced by the Airbus A321LR, a new generation of planes recognized as the most energy efficient in their category. This transition represents a 15% reduction in fuel consumption, 50% less of nitrogen oxide emissions and 50% less noise. 

Transat considers SAF to be a key element in achieving its carbon emissions reduction goal. However, at this time, the volumes of SAF that are produced are not meeting the needs of the industry and, in Canada, SAF is still not commercially produced. Conscious of the important role we can play in the development of a local SAF industry, we signed a long-term SAF purchase agreement with the SAF+ Consortium in 2021. The technology used at its first plant located in Montreal will produce synthetic fuel by captu ring CO₂ from industrial sources 

and combining it with Quebec-produced green hydrogen. 

Transat is also relying on a rigorous fuel management program that was deployed in 2004. This program helps improve the fuel efficiency of our flight and ground airline operations. 

Despite significant technological advances in the fields of aeronautics and sustainable fuel production, compensation solutions through the purchase of mandatory and voluntary carbon credits remain necessary to achieve the decarbonization of the industry and are now part of our strategy. In September 2023, in partnership with CHOOOSE, Transat launched its Act on Your Carbon Footprint program. This program gives customers the option of calculating and reducing their travel-related GHG emissions by contributing to climate projects. This program does not replace or minimize Transat's decarbonization commitments. It is a voluntary engagement option for passengers who wish to offset the emissions associated with their travels. 

3.8.3  Responsible Practices 

In order to increase the positive impact within our communities, both here and at destination, the Corporation is committed to establishing and maintaining healthy and mutually beneficial relationships with its employees, partners, suppliers, customers and other key players in the communities in which it operates. 

Responsible sourcing 

As a global leader, we have a duty to use of our influence to evolve sustainable practices. That said, all members of the supply chain have a role to play in helping transform our industry. In this regard, the Corporation relies on the cooperation of all its suppliers and expects them to meet the highest standards of quality and ethics, as defined in its responsible sourcing policy. 

The supply of goods and services is governed by a number of operating philosophies and principles that guide our strategies and practices and which are consistent with Transat's global growth plan. To this end, a formal code of conduct sets out ESG requirements for suppliers who do business with the Corporation. Previously intended for tourism service providers, the code of conduct was revised in 2023 to extend its scope to all Transat suppliers. This review also made it possible to further explain and amend a certain number of elements to better reflect our commitments and our current requirements in relation to the principles defended by the Code of Conduct. Community Engagement 

For several years now, we have been doing more and more philanthropic work with organizations that support causes that are close to our hearts. # Best States Rankings

Some states shine in healthcare. Some soar in education. Some excel in both – or in much more. The Best States rankings by U.S. News draw on thousands of data points to measure how well states are performing for their citizens. In addition to [healthcare](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/health-care) and [education](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/education), the rankings take into account a state’s [economy](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/economy); its [roads, bridges, internet and other infrastructure](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/infrastructure); its [public safety](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/crime-and-corrections); its [natural environment](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/natural-environment); the [fiscal stability](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/fiscal-stability) of state government; and the [opportunity](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/opportunity) it affords its residents.

More weight was accorded to some categories than others, based on a survey of what matters most to people. Healthcare and education were weighted most heavily. Then came state economies, infrastructure, and the opportunity states offer their citizens. Fiscal stability followed closely in weighting, followed by measures of crime and corrections and a state's natural environment.

See the overall Best States rankings below, and check out the Best States [methodology](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/articles/methodology) for a detailed look at the data behind the Best States rankings.

,
With the outbreak of the Mexican-American War, several hundred members formed what became known as the [Mormon Battalion](https://historytogo.utah.gov/mormon-battalion/), which marched from [Kansas](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/kansas) to [San Diego](https://travel.usnews.com/San_Diego_CA/) from 1846 to 1847, forging a wagon route across the deep Southwest.

,
They moved to [Mexico](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-countries/mexico) until the war’s end, returning in 1848 to the place they hoped to make the [state of Deseret](https://blogs.loc.gov/maps/2016/04/the-state-formerly-known-as-deseret/), a name drawing on the symbol of community found in a honey beehive in the Book of Mormon. By 1850, with a population of more than 11,000, church leaders chose members to head their settlements, and through 1900, the [Mormons founded 500 communities](https://historytogo.utah.gov/mormon-settlement/) in Utah and neighboring states.

,
On May 10, 1869, the [first transcontinental railroad](https://www.census.gov/about/history/stories/monthly/2023/may-2023.html) was established at Promontory Summit in the Utah territory, where the Union and Central Pacific Railroads met. As gold and silver were discovered in the mountains, Congress named the territory Utah after local Native Americans. The Utah territory was carved up, with some forming [Nevada](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/nevada), some added to [Colorado](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/colorado) and some to [Wyoming](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/wyoming). Utah became the 45th state in 1896.

,
Utah’s mountains, high plateaus and deserts – containing the [largest saltwater lake](http://www.history.com/topics/us-states/utah) in the Western Hemisphere, at the state capital of [Salt Lake City](https://realestate.usnews.com/places/utah/salt-lake-city) – are bordered by Colorado, [New Mexico](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/new-mexico) and [Arizona](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/arizona) at right angles. The “[Four Corners](https://www.visitutah.com/places-to-go/parks-outdoors/four-corners-area)” are the only such arrangement in the U.S.

,
The state is known for its skiing, with the mountains near [Salt Lake City](https://travel.usnews.com/Salt_Lake_City_UT/) collecting abundant snowfall, as well as for the [Sundance Film Festival](https://www.visitutah.com/things-to-do/events/sundance-film-festival), one of the world’s premiere independent film festivals, staged for years each January in [Park City](https://travel.usnews.com/Park_City_UT/) before its planned [move](https://www.sundance.org/blogs/sundance-institute-announces-boulder-colorado-as-the-new-home-for-the-sundance-film-festival-beginning-in-2027/) to Colorado in 2027.

[![Image 8](https://www.usnews.com/object/image/0000015a-1a1b-d479-a9df-9b3f287e0000/bs17-south-dakota-crop-editorial.jpg?update-time=1486675682442&size=responsiveGallery)](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/south-dakota)### [South Dakota](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/south-dakota) ![Image 9](https://www.usnews.com/static/img/mini-badge-color.svg)**#2**in**Best States Overall** What is now South Dakota was [among the northern Plains land](https://sdsos.gov/general-information/about-state-south-dakota/default.aspx#) claimed by the French and sold to the U.S. in the 1803 Louisiana Purchase.

,
Soon after, [Meriwether Lewis and William Clark](https://history.sd.gov/docs/LewisandClarkTeachManual.pdf) explored the Missouri River stretch of present-day South Dakota, meeting Yankton and Lakota Sioux tribes along the way. In 1861, Yankton was named the capital of the Dakota Territory, which included today’s South and [North Dakota](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/north-dakota) and much of [Wyoming](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/wyoming) and [Montana](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/montana).

,
The [1868 Treaty of Fort Laramie](https://www.archives.gov/milestone-documents/fort-laramie-treaty) granted the Sioux the Black Hills and land in South Dakota, Wyoming and Montana. The U.S. seized the land nine years later, forcing Native Americans to resettle on smaller, dispersed reservations.

,
North and South Dakota were admitted as the 39th and 40th states in 1889. Because of controversy over which state should be signed into the Union first, President Benjamin Harrison did not record the order.

,
Gutzon Borglum began sculpting [Mount Rushmore National Memorial](https://www.nps.gov/moru/learn/historyculture/memorial-history.htm) in 1927. He planned to carve George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Abraham Lincoln and Theodore Roosevelt from head to waist, but died in 1941 before completion. With his death and impending American involvement in World War II, the memorial was declared completed.

,
In 1980 – more than a century after the U.S. broke the Treaty of Fort Laramie and seized Sioux land – the Supreme Court ruled that the government had taken the land illegally and awarded $120.5 million to the Lakota Sioux, who refused to accept payment and instead demanded the territory be returned.

,
Today, [agriculture generates](https://agunited.org/about-us/key-facts/) much of the state’s economic activity. South Dakota also has a [growing tourism industry](https://sdvisit.com/), with Mount Rushmore and the [Badlands National Park](https://www.nps.gov/badl/index.htm) among visitor favorites.

[![Image 13](https://www.usnews.com/object/image/00000177-d0a6-d218-a3ff-ffbf45120000/bs21-minesota-profile.jpg?update-time=1614113406302&size=responsiveGallery)](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/minnesota)### [Minnesota](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/minnesota) ![Image 14](https://www.usnews.com/static/img/mini-badge-color.svg)**#3**in**Best States Overall** The U.S. [gained the land](https://www.minnpost.com/mnopedia/2014/02/story-behind-minnesotas-weirdly-shaped-northern-border/) now known as Minnesota starting in the late 1700s through the Treaty of Paris, the Louisiana Purchase and negotiations with the Dakota Indians and other tribes who had long inhabited the land.

,
The start of Minnesota’s statehood, gained in 1858, was marked by hostile relations between the settlers and the Dakota over [land treaties and mistreatment by traders](https://www.usdakotawar.org/history/treaties/minnesota-treaties). Only a few years later, Minnesota was the [first state to offer its troops to the Union](https://www.mnhs.org/fortsnelling/learn/military-history/civil-war) in the Civil War, though it was the youngest state.

,
As the northernmost territory in the 48 contiguous states, Minnesota is known for its frigid conditions. The cold weather explains ice hockey’s popularity in Minnesota, and makes it a perfect destination for cross-country skiing, ice fishing and other snow sports.

,
The state is also known for its many lakes, which eventually flow into the Hudson Bay, the Atlantic Ocean and the Gulf of Mexico. The headwaters of the Mississippi River start in northern Lake Itasca. The Dakota fittingly named the land “[Minisota](https://www2.startribune.com/mnisota-mni-sota-dakota-language-minnesota-river-state-name/600114154/),” meaning sky-tinted water. The state’s nickname as the Land of 10,000 Lakes is an understatement – the state has more than [11,500](https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/faq/mnfacts/water.html).

,
The [Mayo Clinic](http://www.mayoclinic.org/about-mayo-clinic), a nonprofit health organization, is headquartered in Rochester and is among the state’s top employers. Manufacturing and retail trade are two other major industries in Minnesota, which houses many [Fortune 500 companies](https://mn.gov/deed/dobusiness/why-mn/our-economy/) such as UnitedHealth Group, Target, 3M and General Mills.

,
The Cornhusker State counts corn production as a leading crop, and its “[Golden Triangle](https://nebraskacorn.gov/cornstalk/animals/golden-triangle/)” of corn, livestock and ethanol production drives its industry.

,
A major urban center in the state is Omaha, home to [Warren Buffett](http://www.forbes.com/pictures/mmk45fgld/warren-buffett-house-omaha-nebraska/#35158044645d), one of the world’s richest men. Stock in his [Berkshire Hathaway](http://www.berkshirehathaway.com/) holding company, managing a wide array of companies, has made many Americans wealthy over 50 years.

,
Before its admission to the Union as the 37th state in 1867, the [Nebraska Territory](http://www.history.com/topics/us-states/nebraska) had been sparsely settled. As railroads pushed west, waves of homesteaders started arriving in 1860. [Omaha](https://travel.usnews.com/Omaha_NE/) had been the territorial capital, but the seat of government was moved to Lancaster, later renamed Lincoln following the assassination of President Abraham Lincoln in 1865.

,
The state’s name is derived from [Oto Indian words](https://statesymbolsusa.org/symbol-official-item/nebraska/state-name-origin/origin-nebraska) translated as “flat water,” referring to the Platte River that flows through the state. The Oto had immigrated to the Central Plains from the East just ahead of the first European settlers. The principal [Siouan people](https://history.nebraska.gov/archeology-of-the-sedentary-siouan-tribes-in-nebraska/#) in the territory during the first half of the 1700s were the Omaha and Ponca in the northeast and Oto in the lower Platte Valley.

,
As Europeans arrived, they forged trading alliances, exchanging beaver and other skins for merchandise. Eventually, the Oto were forced along with Missouria tribe members to accept a reservation in Gage County, in 1854. By 1881, settlers acquired that land too and moved the indigenous settlers to [Oklahoma](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/oklahoma).

,
Snowy mountains, deep valleys, lakes and rivers cover the Gem State, which is twice the size of the six New England states combined. A Rocky Mountain state, Idaho is bordered by [Washington](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/washington), [Oregon](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/oregon), [Nevada](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/nevada), [Utah](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/utah), [Montana](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/montana), [Wyoming](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/wyoming) and a small portion of [Canada](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-countries/canada)’s British Columbia.

,
Though Spaniards began exploring the Northwest in 1592, Meriwether Lewis and William Clark were likely the first European-Americans to enter Idaho in 1805. ,
In the mid-19th century, Union and Confederate supporters [fleeing the Civil War](https://theus50.com/idaho/history.php#google_vignette) went west to Idaho, and Mormons flocked to the region to avoid persecution. Today more Mormons live in Idaho than in almost any other state.

,

,
Idaho’s economy shifted [away from mining](https://www.britannica.com/place/Idaho) toward agriculture after it achieved statehood. Some former mining towns began to host resorts, such as the Sun Valley ski resort, which opened in 1936.

### [Florida](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/florida)

![Image 42](https://www.usnews.com/static/img/mini-badge-color.svg)**#8**in**Best States Overall**

Florida attained statehood in 1845, yet not until a pair of railroad barons built lines down the Atlantic and Gulf coasts in the late 1800s and early 1900s did the state take off, spurring the [phenomenal growth](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/economy/growth) of what’s now the third-most populous state.

,
[Henry Flagler](https://flaglermuseum.us/history/florida-east-coast-railway) arrived aboard the first train to Key West, the southernmost point of the U.S., in 1912, marking completion of his Florida East Coast Railway linking the East Coast from north to south. In his path, he left grand hotels – the [Hotel Ponce de Leon](https://travel.usnews.com/hotels/review-Ponce_De_Leon_Hotel_126349/) in St. Augustine, and the [Breakers](https://travel.usnews.com/hotels/review-the_breakers_palm_beach-palm_beach-florida-39737/) and [Royal Poinciana](https://education.pbchistory.org/flagler-era/the-grand-hotels-the-royal-poinciana/) in what became known as Palm Beach. Another Henry – businessman and steamship owner Henry Plant – pushed rail lines down Florida’s West Coast.

,
With [millions of visitors each year](https://www.visitflorida.org/resources/research/research-faq/) to its beaches, major amusement parks centered around Orlando and cruise ships departing from ports on both coasts, tourism is a major contributor to Florida's gross domestic product. The state’s [agriculture industry](https://www.fdacs.gov/Agriculture-Industry/Florida-Agriculture-Overview-and-Statistics) is also robust, with Florida groves producing many of the country’s oranges and a winter vegetable industry that makes agriculture a year-round enterprise.

,
Tourism, which pays a sizable share of the state’s sales tax, also has enabled Florida to remain among the states without a [personal income tax](https://www.bankrate.com/taxes/states-with-no-income-tax/) – adding to the allure of the nation’s leading retirement haven.

,
The state [has](https://dos.fl.gov/florida-facts/quick-facts/) 1,350 miles of coastline and a land mass of 53,630 square miles. It’s 792 miles by land from Pensacola in the far northwestern Panhandle to Key West at the end of the archipelago that stretches south of Miami, and along the way there is no natural elevation higher than 345 feet – on a ridge of the Panhandle. No state has a lower peak.

,
With several large cities, the state also has a [sizable system](https://www.usnews.com/best-colleges/fl) of state universities and community colleges. The [University of Florida](https://www.usnews.com/best-colleges/university-of-florida-1535) in Gainesville and [Florida State University](https://www.usnews.com/best-colleges/florida-state-university-1489) in Tallahassee have been rivaled in enrollment by the [University of South Florida](https://www.usnews.com/best-colleges/university-of-south-florida-1537) in Tampa, [University of Central Florida](https://www.usnews.com/best-colleges/ucf-3954) in Orlando, and [Florida International University](https://www.usnews.com/best-colleges/fiu-9635) in Miami. Among the best known private institutions is [University of Miami](https://www.usnews.com/best-colleges/university-of-miami-1536).

After the French were defeated in the French and Indian War, [Vermonters declared their independence](http://www.history.com/topics/us-states/vermont) from England separately from the original 13 colonies – though the Continental Congress did not recognize this separation.

,
Among Vermont’s most famous contributions to the American Revolution is the “[Green Mountain Boys](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Green-Mountain-Boys),’’ a band of patriots led by Ethan Allen who formed a militia to fight in the war and later became some of the founding fathers of the state. After 14 years as a self-declared independent republic, Vermont was admitted to the Union as the [14th state in 1791](https://vermonthistoryexplorer.org/the-14th-state).

,
The sweetest product of Vermont’s forests is its renowned maple syrup, the purest labeled “Grade A.” Vermont is one of the [country’s biggest producers](https://www.uvm.edu/extension/maple-statistics) of the sweetener.

,
A [dairy-producing state](https://agriculture.vermont.gov/milk-matters-%E2%80%8B-vermont-dairy-farming-important-us-all), its most famous brand is [Ben & Jerry’s Ice Cream](http://www.benjerry.com/about-us/factory-tours), which was founded in the northern city of Burlington, situated on Lake Champlain, in 1978. Another home-grown Vermont product made founder [Robert Stiller](http://www.forbes.com/profile/robert-stiller/) a billionaire – [Green Mountain Coffee Roasters](https://www.keurig.com/content/greenmountaincoffee), made popular nationally in pods for Keurig coffee-makers.

# Best States Rankings

Some states shine in healthcare. Some soar in education. Some excel in both – or in much more. The Best States rankings by U.S. News draw on thousands of data points to measure how well states are performing for their citizens. In addition to [healthcare](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/health-care) and [education](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/education), the rankings take into account a state’s [economy](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/economy); its [roads, bridges, internet and other infrastructure](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/infrastructure); its [public safety](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/crime-and-corrections); its [natural environment](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/natural-environment); the [fiscal stability](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/fiscal-stability) of state government; and the [opportunity](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/rankings/opportunity) it affords its residents.

More weight was accorded to some categories than others, based on a survey of what matters most to people. Healthcare and education were weighted most heavily. Then came state economies, infrastructure, and the opportunity states offer their citizens. Fiscal stability followed closely in weighting, followed by measures of crime and corrections and a state's natural environment.

See the overall Best States rankings below, and check out the Best States [methodology](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/articles/methodology) for a detailed look at the data behind the Best States rankings.

,
With the outbreak of the Mexican-American War, several hundred members formed what became known as the [Mormon Battalion](https://historytogo.utah.gov/mormon-battalion/), which marched from [Kansas](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/kansas) to [San Diego](https://travel.usnews.com/San_Diego_CA/) from 1846 to 1847, forging a wagon route across the deep Southwest.

,
They moved to [Mexico](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-countries/mexico) until the war’s end, returning in 1848 to the place they hoped to make the [state of Deseret](https://blogs.loc.gov/maps/2016/04/the-state-formerly-known-as-deseret/), a name drawing on the symbol of community found in a honey beehive in the Book of Mormon. By 1850, with a population of more than 11,000, church leaders chose members to head their settlements, and through 1900, the [Mormons founded 500 communities](https://historytogo.utah.gov/mormon-settlement/) in Utah and neighboring states.

,
On May 10, 1869, the [first transcontinental railroad](https://www.census.gov/about/history/stories/monthly/2023/may-2023.html) was established at Promontory Summit in the Utah territory, where the Union and Central Pacific Railroads met. As gold and silver were discovered in the mountains, Congress named the territory Utah after local Native Americans. The Utah territory was carved up, with some forming [Nevada](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/nevada), some added to [Colorado](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/colorado) and some to [Wyoming](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/wyoming). Utah became the 45th state in 1896.

,
Utah’s mountains, high plateaus and deserts – containing the [largest saltwater lake](http://www.history.com/topics/us-states/utah) in the Western Hemisphere, at the state capital of [Salt Lake City](https://realestate.usnews.com/places/utah/salt-lake-city) – are bordered by Colorado, [New Mexico](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/new-mexico) and [Arizona](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/arizona) at right angles. The “[Four Corners](https://www.visitutah.com/places-to-go/parks-outdoors/four-corners-area)” are the only such arrangement in the U.S.

,
The state is known for its skiing, with the mountains near [Salt Lake City](https://travel.usnews.com/Salt_Lake_City_UT/) collecting abundant snowfall, as well as for the [Sundance Film Festival](https://www.visitutah.com/things-to-do/events/sundance-film-festival), one of the world’s premiere independent film festivals, staged for years each January in [Park City](https://travel.usnews.com/Park_City_UT/) before its planned [move](https://www.sundance.org/blogs/sundance-institute-announces-boulder-colorado-as-the-new-home-for-the-sundance-film-festival-beginning-in-2027/) to Colorado in 2027.

[![Image 8](https://www.usnews.com/object/image/0000015a-1a1b-d479-a9df-9b3f287e0000/bs17-south-dakota-crop-editorial.jpg?update-time=1486675682442&size=responsiveGallery)](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/south-dakota)### [South Dakota](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/south-dakota) ![Image 9](https://www.usnews.com/static/img/mini-badge-color.svg)**#2**in**Best States Overall** What is now South Dakota was [among the northern Plains land](https://sdsos.gov/general-information/about-state-south-dakota/default.aspx#) claimed by the French and sold to the U.S. in the 1803 Louisiana Purchase.

,
Soon after, [Meriwether Lewis and William Clark](https://history.sd.gov/docs/LewisandClarkTeachManual.pdf) explored the Missouri River stretch of present-day South Dakota, meeting Yankton and Lakota Sioux tribes along the way. In 1861, Yankton was named the capital of the Dakota Territory, which included today’s South and [North Dakota](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/north-dakota) and much of [Wyoming](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/wyoming) and [Montana](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/montana).

,
The [1868 Treaty of Fort Laramie](https://www.archives.gov/milestone-documents/fort-laramie-treaty) granted the Sioux the Black Hills and land in South Dakota, Wyoming and Montana. The U.S. seized the land nine years later, forcing Native Americans to resettle on smaller, dispersed reservations.

,
North and South Dakota were admitted as the 39th and 40th states in 1889. Because of controversy over which state should be signed into the Union first, President Benjamin Harrison did not record the order.

,
Gutzon Borglum began sculpting [Mount Rushmore National Memorial](https://www.nps.gov/moru/learn/historyculture/memorial-history.htm) in 1927. He planned to carve George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Abraham Lincoln and Theodore Roosevelt from head to waist, but died in 1941 before completion. With his death and impending American involvement in World War II, the memorial was declared completed.

,
In 1980 – more than a century after the U.S. broke the Treaty of Fort Laramie and seized Sioux land – the Supreme Court ruled that the government had taken the land illegally and awarded $120.5 million to the Lakota Sioux, who refused to accept payment and instead demanded the territory be returned.

,
Today, [agriculture generates](https://agunited.org/about-us/key-facts/) much of the state’s economic activity. South Dakota also has a [growing tourism industry](https://sdvisit.com/), with Mount Rushmore and the [Badlands National Park](https://www.nps.gov/badl/index.htm) among visitor favorites.

[![Image 13](https://www.usnews.com/object/image/00000177-d0a6-d218-a3ff-ffbf45120000/bs21-minesota-profile.jpg?update-time=1614113406302&size=responsiveGallery)](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/minnesota)### [Minnesota](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/minnesota) ![Image 14](https://www.usnews.com/static/img/mini-badge-color.svg)**#3**in**Best States Overall** The U.S. [gained the land](https://www.minnpost.com/mnopedia/2014/02/story-behind-minnesotas-weirdly-shaped-northern-border/) now known as Minnesota starting in the late 1700s through the Treaty of Paris, the Louisiana Purchase and negotiations with the Dakota Indians and other tribes who had long inhabited the land.

,
The start of Minnesota’s statehood, gained in 1858, was marked by hostile relations between the settlers and the Dakota over [land treaties and mistreatment by traders](https://www.usdakotawar.org/history/treaties/minnesota-treaties). Only a few years later, Minnesota was the [first state to offer its troops to the Union](https://www.mnhs.org/fortsnelling/learn/military-history/civil-war) in the Civil War, though it was the youngest state.

,
As the northernmost territory in the 48 contiguous states, Minnesota is known for its frigid conditions. The cold weather explains ice hockey’s popularity in Minnesota, and makes it a perfect destination for cross-country skiing, ice fishing and other snow sports.

,
The state is also known for its many lakes, which eventually flow into the Hudson Bay, the Atlantic Ocean and the Gulf of Mexico. The headwaters of the Mississippi River start in northern Lake Itasca. The Dakota fittingly named the land “[Minisota](https://www2.startribune.com/mnisota-mni-sota-dakota-language-minnesota-river-state-name/600114154/),” meaning sky-tinted water. The state’s nickname as the Land of 10,000 Lakes is an understatement – the state has more than [11,500](https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/faq/mnfacts/water.html).

,
The [Mayo Clinic](http://www.mayoclinic.org/about-mayo-clinic), a nonprofit health organization, is headquartered in Rochester and is among the state’s top employers. Manufacturing and retail trade are two other major industries in Minnesota, which houses many [Fortune 500 companies](https://mn.gov/deed/dobusiness/why-mn/our-economy/) such as UnitedHealth Group, Target, 3M and General Mills.

Snowy mountains, deep valleys, lakes and rivers cover the Gem State, which is twice the size of the six New England states combined. A Rocky Mountain state, Idaho is bordered by [Washington](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/washington), [Oregon](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/oregon), [Nevada](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/nevada), [Utah](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/utah), [Montana](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/montana), [Wyoming](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/wyoming) and a small portion of [Canada](https://www.usnews.com/news/best-countries/canada)’s British Columbia.

,

,
Idaho’s economy shifted [away from mining](https://www.britannica.com/place/Idaho) toward agriculture after it achieved statehood. Some former mining towns began to host resorts, such as the Sun Valley ski resort, which opened in 1936.

,
[Henry Flagler](https://flaglermuseum.us/history/florida-east-coast-railway) arrived aboard the first train to Key West, the southernmost point of the U.S., in 1912, marking completion of his Florida East Coast Railway linking the East Coast from north to south. In his path, he left grand hotels – the [Hotel Ponce de Leon](https://travel.usnews.com/hotels/review-Ponce_De_Leon_Hotel_126349/) in St. Augustine, and the [Breakers](https://travel.usnews.com/hotels/review-the_breakers_palm_beach-palm_beach-florida-39737/) and [Royal Poinciana](https://education.pbchistory.org/flagler-era/the-grand-hotels-the-royal-poinciana/) in what became known as Palm Beach. Another Henry – businessman and steamship owner Henry Plant – pushed rail lines down Florida’s West Coast.

,
With [millions of visitors each year](https://www.visitflorida.org/resources/research/research-faq/) to its beaches, major amusement parks centered around Orlando and cruise ships departing from ports on both coasts, tourism is a major contributor to Florida's gross domestic product. The state’s [agriculture industry](https://www.fdacs.gov/Agriculture-Industry/Florida-Agriculture-Overview-and-Statistics) is also robust, with Florida groves producing many of the country’s oranges and a winter vegetable industry that makes agriculture a year-round enterprise.

,
Tourism, which pays a sizable share of the state’s sales tax, also has enabled Florida to remain among the states without a [personal income tax](https://www.bankrate.com/taxes/states-with-no-income-tax/) – adding to the allure of the nation’s leading retirement haven.

,

Among the best known private institutions is [University of Miami](https://www.usnews.com/best-colleges/university-of-miami-1536).

I recently accomplished my life goal of visiting all 50 states.

People naturally ask, “What was your favorite?”

It’s so tough to pick a favorite. This is an incredible country with diverse cultures, experiences and topographical features.

I decided to rank all 50 states, not only on my opinion but on several other factors related to tourism:

*   Affordability (with a higher weight on sales tax)
*   Natural Beauty ([as judged by Thrillist](https://www.thrillist.com/travel/nation/most-beautiful-states-in-america))
*   State and National Park coverage ([source](https://www.playgroundequipment.com/us-states-ranked-by-state-and-national-park-coverage/))
*   Food and drink quality ([as ranked by Far & Wide](https://www.farandwide.com/s/us-states-ranked-food-2f86e72cb89c4904))
*   Overall popularity ([source](https://www.simplemost.com/most-least-favorite-us-states-vacation/))

I averaged all these rankings (along with my personal rank) and below are the results, going from worst to best…

## 50. Kansas

Kansas City is amazing, but unfortunately the lion’s share of it is in Missouri. So, I guess you could visit Wichita?

## 49. North Dakota

I filmed my first impression of North Dakota and linked it below. Spoiler alert: it was uninspiring. ## 8. Alaska

*   Hike in Denali National Park
*   Go salmon fishing near Cooper Landing
*   Do a whale watching cruise to Kenai Fjords National Park

I recently accomplished my life goal of visiting all 50 states.

People naturally ask, “What was your favorite?”

It’s so tough to pick a favorite. This is an incredible country with diverse cultures, experiences and topographical features.

I decided to rank all 50 states, not only on my opinion but on several other factors related to tourism:

*   Affordability (with a higher weight on sales tax)
*   Natural Beauty ([as judged by Thrillist](https://www.thrillist.com/travel/nation/most-beautiful-states-in-america))
*   State and National Park coverage ([source](https://www.playgroundequipment.com/us-states-ranked-by-state-and-national-park-coverage/))
*   Food and drink quality ([as ranked by Far & Wide](https://www.farandwide.com/s/us-states-ranked-food-2f86e72cb89c4904))
*   Overall popularity ([source](https://www.simplemost.com/most-least-favorite-us-states-vacation/))

I averaged all these rankings (along with my personal rank) and below are the results, going from worst to best…

## 50. Kansas

Kansas City is amazing, but unfortunately the lion’s share of it is in Missouri. So, I guess you could visit Wichita?

![Image 4](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:615/1*LNsKID1cqwiWI5QOkBz7CQ.jpeg)

## 49. North Dakota

I filmed my first impression of North Dakota and linked it below. Spoiler alert: it was uninspiring. # I’ve Been to All 50 States. These Are the Bottom 25

I’ve been to all 50 States. How would I rank them?

Before moving to France, we traveled around the U.S. for two years in our RAV4. When mentioning this to friends, family, and strangers, by far the most common questions that come up are, “What are your favorite/least favorite states?”

Normally, I answer pretty diplomatically and wait until the person gets bored with the question they just asked. I don’t want to tell you that your favorite state sucks. I also don’t want to hear you hate on my favorites.

I’m putting all of that aside here with the help of my favorite tool, the Excel spreadsheet. Yup. I used math to rank the best (and the worst) because that’s what I do. So here we go!

## My Methodology

A quick Google search will lead you to plenty of people making their own lists of the worst states to visit. But few (if any) have gone to the lengths I have to give you a less subjective list.

I looked at four major categories to bring you the best of the best and the worst of the worst.

Here’s what I considered in my states ranked worst to best.

[](https://giphy.com/gifs/ifhtfilms-confused-math-numbers-lHfxDepSGlzom6f65K)

### What can you do outside while you’re there?

Aside from counting the number of state and/or national parks, I also wanted to include visual beauty.

For example, Florida has over 250 state parks. But I wouldn’t say that means they are better than South Dakota, a state with actual topography to look at, but only 16 State parks. To do this, I used some existing rankings online and my own personal thoughts.

### What’s the food scene like?

**Less than 10 states have Michelin-starred restaurants —sorry, Massachusetts —so I can’t just use that metric.**

To help balance that out, I contemplated things like population density, percentages of immigrants, and percentages of people who were from other states in my rankings.

### What’s the sports and culture scene like?

Not every state has a pro sports team, so outside of the major sports teams, how many significant college sports programs are there for you to watch? Do they also have something like Pioneer Days in Cheyenne that no other state has?

**I also considered the broader cultural scene.**How many museums, music venues, theaters, and annual festivals are there? Are there state fairs, food festivals, or local traditions that people look forward to each year?

All of those things make places better, in my opinion.

### How did my personal experiences factor in?

**Visiting all 50 states means you get to have an opinion about those places.**While numbers still mattered, I still kept a pretty biased list based on gut feelings and personal experiences. They weren’t all winners, and that’s OK.

From there, I ranked them 1-50 in each of the four categories and averaged them all out in my spreadsheet. Let’s see how it shook out!

Prefer video? Check out our March Madness-style take on the best (and worst) U.S. states.

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BLPmP2cfTW8)

## #50: North Dakota

![Image 3: A buffalo munches on grass in a North Dakota park.](https://www.travelonthereg.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/North-Dakota-Wildlife-800x600.webp)
Why is the “top” Dakota in last place, you ask? Well, aside from “things you can do outside,” thanks to [Teddy Roosevelt National Park](https://www.travelonthereg.com/theodore-roosevelt-national-park-itinerary/), they come in last or second-to-last in every other category on my spreadsheet.

They actually have the second-lowest total of parks for you to explore, so it’s not even outside of the bottom 10 in this category.**It is the coldest state in the lower 48, as well, so be prepared for a short travel season.**

No “major” sports or college teams are based here — [sorry, Fargo](https://www.travelonthereg.com/things-to-do-in-fargo/) — and their low population doesn’t give you many museums, events, festivals, and other activities to attend. The food also suffers from a lack of diversity.

Unfortunately, someone has to be last, and we salute you, redundant Dakota!

## #49: Nebraska

![Image 4: A dog poses at a national monument in Nebraska.](https://www.travelonthereg.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Nebraska-Monument.webp)

Next up is Warren Buffett’s home state. They “beat” North Dakota in every category but playing outside, thanks to [Warren’s city of Omaha](https://www.travelonthereg.com/one-day-in-omaha/). **The city has better food and entertainment than all of North Dakota.**

They also have the Huskers to root for, which is as major a college sporting program as you can get.

Outside of [Omaha](https://www.stay22.com/allez/roam?aid=travelonthereg&campaign=travelonthereg-bottom25statesranked&product=lma&habl=false&isinc=true&sid22=l7yEtHJW8e1M8QEx&adStack=mediavine&hasCTZ=false&hasTP=false&conmeth=tzmm&plng=en-US&pageCategory=travel&source=direct&medium=hyperlink&address=Omaha%2C+Nebraska%2C+USA&search=Omaha&category=accommodation&sparkLinkId=904269e3-ac60-4f66-849a-c0e8617aa491&ref22=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.travelonthereg.com%2Fbottom-25-states-ranked) and Lincoln, there aren’t a lot of things to see and do, but [Scotts Bluff](https://www.stay22.com/allez/roam?aid=travelonthereg&campaign=travelonthereg-bottom25statesranked&product=lma&habl=false&isinc=true&sid22=l7yEtHJW8e1M8QEx&adStack=mediavine&hasCTZ=false&hasTP=false&conmeth=tzmm&plng=en-US&pageCategory=travel&source=direct&medium=hyperlink&address=Scotts+Bluff%2C+Nebraska%2C+USA&search=Scotts+Bluff&category=accommodation&sparkLinkId=a9b3e179-468d-4c9d-bf96-e6c141967742&ref22=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.travelonthereg.com%2Fbottom-25-states-ranked) did provide us with a fun escape from our month-long stay in Cheyenne.

You can also walk from Nebraska to Iowa on the Bob Kerrey Pedestrian Bridge in Omaha. At the midpoint, you’re actually standing in both states at once.

One last plus: Nebraska is closer to the Denver International Airport than Denver actually is.

I kid, Denver airport, I kid.

## #48: Kansas

[Video 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zvQT-tBbDFE)

Agnes hasn’t written a blog post about anything we did in Kansas, so this feels right. There’s Dodge City for some Wyatt Earp history, and you can also go over the Missouri border to the superior “Kansas City” for barbecue.

> Fun fact: A 2003 study by Arizona State and SW Texas State found that Kansas was flatter than an IHOP pancake. While the study has since been debunked, they were the first state to be scientifically compared to a pancake in a published study.

So why isn’t Kansas lower, you ask? First of all, how dare you question my rankings already?

Second, Kansas does have a few major college sports programs, as well as being just across the river from the Chiefs (for now) and Royals.

**Being closer to an actual metropolitan area also brings more access to the arts and food you won’t find in the first two on my list.**That being said, put Kansas lower on your list if it feels right to you.

## #47 (tie): Delaware

![Image 5: A woman on a bench at a Delaware beach](https://www.travelonthereg.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Delaware-Beaches.webp)

My own biased personal ranking and the food category are what make Delaware higher up than the first three on this list.

I’m going to be honest, though. I don’t remember seeing a whole lot in Delaware. It’s the second smallest state after Rhode Island, so maybe I took a nap during our drive through on our way to see the horses on Assateague Island.

I also had too many beers at the Dogfish Head Brewery.

[](https://giphy.com/gifs/waynes-world-party-time-EV0cGckwbnRG8)

Wilmington is just down the river from Philadelphia, though, and the DC/Baltimore area provides a good base should you wish to “tick” this one off your 50-state list.

Delaware was the first state to ratify the U.S. Constitution, by the way, so they try to bring attention to the fact that there isn’t much of anything else to do here by bragging that they are “The First State.”

## #47 (tie): South Dakota

![Image 6: A view of the Badlands in South Dakota](https://www.travelonthereg.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/South-Dakota-Badlands-800x600.webp)
The “bottom” Dakota shines in outdoor activities like [The Badlands](https://www.travelonthereg.com/badlands-national-park-itinerary/), The Black Hills, [Mount Rushmore](https://www.travelonthereg.com/is-mount-rushmore-worth-visiting/), [Custer State Park](https://www.travelonthereg.com/custer-state-park-wildlife-loop/), and Wind Cave National Park.

There are even “unique” “cultural” activities like the Sturgis Motorcycle Rally, and tourist trap [gold rush cities like Deadwood](https://www.travelonthereg.com/is-deadwood-worth-visiting/), Lead, and Spearfish if you so desire.

Outside of these (mostly) awesome things, South Dakota just doesn’t have it for food, sports/entertainment, and my own personal bias against states annoying to travel to. It is also mostly flat until you go west over the Missouri River.

> Note: If you hate the ocean, the point in the United States that is furthest from it is located in South Dakota. It’s just over 1,000 miles from the nearest coastline.

I’m going to be honest with you here. My spreadsheet led me astray with this one. My former insurance career brought me to New Jersey several times before I was able to visit for my own enjoyment, though, so this might taint my negative view a little bit.

My own personal thoughts of New Jersey aside, there’s plenty to see and do here and nearby. I mean, it’s right across the river from one of the greatest cities in the world!

Within New Jersey, you, of course, can get your East Coast Vegas fix in Atlantic City. While there, stroll along the coast made (more?) famous by some reality show Italian-Americans.

**Perhaps most importantly, the best cheesesteak I’ve ever eaten was not in Philly, but in Camden, at Donkey’s Place.**If you don’t trust me, Anthony Bourdain agreed with me at least.

## #27: Alaska

![Image 28: A man takes a picture of a mushroom in Alaska.](https://www.travelonthereg.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Alaska-Photo-Stop.webp)

Another spreadsheet killer here in Alaska. I guess the low population, lack of sports teams, and the fact that it’s slightly hard to get to offset the part about this being probably the best state visually to go see.

I mean, where else can you watch glaciers calve into the sea?!? **That’s a regular thing at Alaska’s tidewater glaciers, especially around places like Kenai Fjords near Seward.**

Between [driving from Anchorage to Seward](https://www.travelonthereg.com/drive-from-anchorage-to-seward/), exploring [Denali National Park](https://www.travelonthereg.com/denali-national-park-itinerary/), and spotting wildlife between [Anchorage and Denali](https://www.travelonthereg.com/drive-from-anchorage-to-denali/), the scenery makes this place unreal.

Definitely go here. This list is wrong and stupid.

## #26: South Carolina

![Image 29: A statue outside of a golf shop in South Carolina](https://www.travelonthereg.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/South-Carolina-Golf.webp)

Last up on the back half is the bottom Carolina. No, I don’t know why it’s above Alaska either.

**Smaller Carolina has all kinds of things travelers would want: mountains in the west, beaches in the east, golf resorts all over, history, and excellent southern food.**

[Charleston](https://www.stay22.com/allez/roam?aid=travelonthereg&campaign=travelonthereg-bottom25statesranked&product=lma&habl=false&isinc=true&sid22=l7yEtHJW8e1M8QEx&adStack=mediavine&hasCTZ=false&hasTP=false&conmeth=tzmm&plng=en-US&pageCategory=travel&source=direct&medium=hyperlink&address=Charleston%2C+South+Carolina%2C+USA&search=Charleston&category=accommodation&sparkLinkId=abdbd098-48df-46e1-ae8f-1b939a01aa08&ref22=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.travelonthereg.com%2Fbottom-25-states-ranked) is another one of my [favorite Southern cities to visit](https://www.travelonthereg.com/one-day-in-charleston/). Take a food/walking tour there, and you’ll see what I mean.

Speaking of walking, I would go to Myrtle Beach and Hilton Head as much as Agnes would let me to golf. Maybe not to Kiawah, though, because boy was that pricey.

If golf isn’t your thing, the state has a surprisingly cool national park. [Congaree National Park](https://www.travelonthereg.com/things-to-do-in-congaree-national-park/) protects one of the largest intact bottomland hardwood forests in the country, with boardwalk trails through massive old-growth trees and peaceful kayaking.

# I’ve Been to All 50 States. These Are the Bottom 25

I’ve been to all 50 States. How would I rank them?

Before moving to France, we traveled around the U.S. for two years in our RAV4. When mentioning this to friends, family, and strangers, by far the most common questions that come up are, “What are your favorite/least favorite states?”

Normally, I answer pretty diplomatically and wait until the person gets bored with the question they just asked. I don’t want to tell you that your favorite state sucks. I also don’t want to hear you hate on my favorites.

I’m putting all of that aside here with the help of my favorite tool, the Excel spreadsheet. Yup. I used math to rank the best (and the worst) because that’s what I do. So here we go!

## My Methodology

A quick Google search will lead you to plenty of people making their own lists of the worst states to visit. But few (if any) have gone to the lengths I have to give you a less subjective list.

I looked at four major categories to bring you the best of the best and the worst of the worst.

Here’s what I considered in my states ranked worst to best.

[](https://giphy.com/gifs/ifhtfilms-confused-math-numbers-lHfxDepSGlzom6f65K)

### What can you do outside while you’re there?

Aside from counting the number of state and/or national parks, I also wanted to include visual beauty.

For example, Florida has over 250 state parks. But I wouldn’t say that means they are better than South Dakota, a state with actual topography to look at, but only 16 State parks. To do this, I used some existing rankings online and my own personal thoughts.

### What’s the food scene like?

**Less than 10 states have Michelin-starred restaurants —sorry, Massachusetts —so I can’t just use that metric.**

To help balance that out, I contemplated things like population density, percentages of immigrants, and percentages of people who were from other states in my rankings.

### What’s the sports and culture scene like?

Not every state has a pro sports team, so outside of the major sports teams, how many significant college sports programs are there for you to watch? Do they also have something like Pioneer Days in Cheyenne that no other state has?

**I also considered the broader cultural scene.**How many museums, music venues, theaters, and annual festivals are there? Are there state fairs, food festivals, or local traditions that people look forward to each year?

All of those things make places better, in my opinion.

### How did my personal experiences factor in?

**Visiting all 50 states means you get to have an opinion about those places.**While numbers still mattered, I still kept a pretty biased list based on gut feelings and personal experiences. They weren’t all winners, and that’s OK.

From there, I ranked them 1-50 in each of the four categories and averaged them all out in my spreadsheet. Let’s see how it shook out!

Prefer video? Check out our March Madness-style take on the best (and worst) U.S. states.

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BLPmP2cfTW8)

## #50: North Dakota

![Image 3: A buffalo munches on grass in a North Dakota park.](https://www.travelonthereg.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/North-Dakota-Wildlife-800x600.webp)
Why is the “top” Dakota in last place, you ask? Well, aside from “things you can do outside,” thanks to [Teddy Roosevelt National Park](https://www.travelonthereg.com/theodore-roosevelt-national-park-itinerary/), they come in last or second-to-last in every other category on my spreadsheet.

They actually have the second-lowest total of parks for you to explore, so it’s not even outside of the bottom 10 in this category.**It is the coldest state in the lower 48, as well, so be prepared for a short travel season.**

No “major” sports or college teams are based here — [sorry, Fargo](https://www.travelonthereg.com/things-to-do-in-fargo/) — and their low population doesn’t give you many museums, events, festivals, and other activities to attend. The food also suffers from a lack of diversity.

Unfortunately, someone has to be last, and we salute you, redundant Dakota!

## #49: Nebraska

![Image 4: A dog poses at a national monument in Nebraska.](https://www.travelonthereg.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Nebraska-Monument.webp)

Next up is Warren Buffett’s home state. They “beat” North Dakota in every category but playing outside, thanks to [Warren’s city of Omaha](https://www.travelonthereg.com/one-day-in-omaha/). **The city has better food and entertainment than all of North Dakota.**

They also have the Huskers to root for, which is as major a college sporting program as you can get.

Outside of [Omaha](https://www.stay22.com/allez/roam?aid=travelonthereg&campaign=travelonthereg-bottom25statesranked&product=lma&habl=false&isinc=true&sid22=l7yEtHJW8e1M8QEx&adStack=mediavine&hasCTZ=false&hasTP=false&conmeth=tzmm&plng=en-US&pageCategory=travel&source=direct&medium=hyperlink&address=Omaha%2C+Nebraska%2C+USA&search=Omaha&category=accommodation&sparkLinkId=904269e3-ac60-4f66-849a-c0e8617aa491&ref22=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.travelonthereg.com%2Fbottom-25-states-ranked) and Lincoln, there aren’t a lot of things to see and do, but [Scotts Bluff](https://www.stay22.com/allez/roam?aid=travelonthereg&campaign=travelonthereg-bottom25statesranked&product=lma&habl=false&isinc=true&sid22=l7yEtHJW8e1M8QEx&adStack=mediavine&hasCTZ=false&hasTP=false&conmeth=tzmm&plng=en-US&pageCategory=travel&source=direct&medium=hyperlink&address=Scotts+Bluff%2C+Nebraska%2C+USA&search=Scotts+Bluff&category=accommodation&sparkLinkId=a9b3e179-468d-4c9d-bf96-e6c141967742&ref22=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.travelonthereg.com%2Fbottom-25-states-ranked) did provide us with a fun escape from our month-long stay in Cheyenne.

You can also walk from Nebraska to Iowa on the Bob Kerrey Pedestrian Bridge in Omaha. At the midpoint, you’re actually standing in both states at once.

One last plus: Nebraska is closer to the Denver International Airport than Denver actually is.

I kid, Denver airport, I kid.

## #48: Kansas

[Video 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zvQT-tBbDFE)

Agnes hasn’t written a blog post about anything we did in Kansas, so this feels right. There’s Dodge City for some Wyatt Earp history, and you can also go over the Missouri border to the superior “Kansas City” for barbecue.

> Fun fact: A 2003 study by Arizona State and SW Texas State found that Kansas was flatter than an IHOP pancake. While the study has since been debunked, they were the first state to be scientifically compared to a pancake in a published study.

So why isn’t Kansas lower, you ask? First of all, how dare you question my rankings already?

Second, Kansas does have a few major college sports programs, as well as being just across the river from the Chiefs (for now) and Royals.

**Being closer to an actual metropolitan area also brings more access to the arts and food you won’t find in the first two on my list.**That being said, put Kansas lower on your list if it feels right to you.

## #47 (tie): Delaware

![Image 5: A woman on a bench at a Delaware beach](https://www.travelonthereg.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Delaware-Beaches.webp)

My own biased personal ranking and the food category are what make Delaware higher up than the first three on this list.

I’m going to be honest, though. I don’t remember seeing a whole lot in Delaware. It’s the second smallest state after Rhode Island, so maybe I took a nap during our drive through on our way to see the horses on Assateague Island.

I also had too many beers at the Dogfish Head Brewery.

[](https://giphy.com/gifs/waynes-world-party-time-EV0cGckwbnRG8)

Wilmington is just down the river from Philadelphia, though, and the DC/Baltimore area provides a good base should you wish to “tick” this one off your 50-state list.

The “bottom” Dakota shines in outdoor activities like [The Badlands](https://www.travelonthereg.com/badlands-national-park-itinerary/), The Black Hills, [Mount Rushmore](https://www.travelonthereg.com/is-mount-rushmore-worth-visiting/), [Custer State Park](https://www.travelonthereg.com/custer-state-park-wildlife-loop/), and Wind Cave National Park.

The southern end of the state contains natural beauty in the Ozarks. Nearby is the resort city of Branson, and if you are scoffing at the “resort” title, I encourage you to open your mind (and wallet) to experience what this town has to offer.

## #29: Vermont

![Image 26: Downtown Montpelier in Vermont](https://www.travelonthereg.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Vermont-Montpelier-800x600.webp)
Next up is Maine’s “almost” neighbor, Vermont. Much like a lot of the Northeastern United States, Vermont has some excellent scenery in the fall.

In addition, they have some cool [mountain towns like Stowe](https://www.travelonthereg.com/things-to-do-in-stowe-vermont/) and one of the most scenic capital cities, Montpelier.

It’s also home to [Dog Mountain near St. Johnsbury](https://www.travelonthereg.com/dog-mountain-vermont/). It’s a 150-acre dog paradise where pups can roam free or visit the Dog Chapel, a place dedicated to the bond between people and their pets.

Kimmy would probably rank this state closer to the top if she had a vote.

> Note: We’ve been to three places named Montpelier now, and I think each one is spelled and pronounced differently.

## #28: New Jersey

![Image 27: A man gets ready to eat some meat in Camden, New Jersey.](https://www.travelonthereg.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/New-Jersey-Barbecue.webp)

I’m going to be honest with you here. My spreadsheet led me astray with this one. My former insurance career brought me to New Jersey several times before I was able to visit for my own enjoyment, though, so this might taint my negative view a little bit.

My own personal thoughts of New Jersey aside, there’s plenty to see and do here and nearby. I mean, it’s right across the river from one of the greatest cities in the world!

Within New Jersey, you, of course, can get your East Coast Vegas fix in Atlantic City. While there, stroll along the coast made (more?) famous by some reality show Italian-Americans.

**Perhaps most importantly, the best cheesesteak I’ve ever eaten was not in Philly, but in Camden, at Donkey’s Place.**If you don’t trust me, Anthony Bourdain agreed with me at least.

## #27: Alaska

![Image 28: A man takes a picture of a mushroom in Alaska.](https://www.travelonthereg.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Alaska-Photo-Stop.webp)

Another spreadsheet killer here in Alaska. I guess the low population, lack of sports teams, and the fact that it’s slightly hard to get to offset the part about this being probably the best state visually to go see.

I mean, where else can you watch glaciers calve into the sea?!? **That’s a regular thing at Alaska’s tidewater glaciers, especially around places like Kenai Fjords near Seward.**

Between [driving from Anchorage to Seward](https://www.travelonthereg.com/drive-from-anchorage-to-seward/), exploring [Denali National Park](https://www.travelonthereg.com/denali-national-park-itinerary/), and spotting wildlife between [Anchorage and Denali](https://www.travelonthereg.com/drive-from-anchorage-to-denali/), the scenery makes this place unreal.

Definitely go here. This list is wrong and stupid.

## #26: South Carolina

![Image 29: A statue outside of a golf shop in South Carolina](https://www.travelonthereg.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/South-Carolina-Golf.webp)

Last up on the back half is the bottom Carolina. No, I don’t know why it’s above Alaska either.

**Smaller Carolina has all kinds of things travelers would want: mountains in the west, beaches in the east, golf resorts all over, history, and excellent southern food.**

[Charleston](https://www.stay22.com/allez/roam?aid=travelonthereg&campaign=travelonthereg-bottom25statesranked&product=lma&habl=false&isinc=true&sid22=l7yEtHJW8e1M8QEx&adStack=mediavine&hasCTZ=false&hasTP=false&conmeth=tzmm&plng=en-US&pageCategory=travel&source=direct&medium=hyperlink&address=Charleston%2C+South+Carolina%2C+USA&search=Charleston&category=accommodation&sparkLinkId=abdbd098-48df-46e1-ae8f-1b939a01aa08&ref22=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.travelonthereg.com%2Fbottom-25-states-ranked) is another one of my [favorite Southern cities to visit](https://www.travelonthereg.com/one-day-in-charleston/). Take a food/walking tour there, and you’ll see what I mean.

Speaking of walking, I would go to Myrtle Beach and Hilton Head as much as Agnes would let me to golf. Maybe not to Kiawah, though, because boy was that pricey.

If golf isn’t your thing, the state has a surprisingly cool national park. [Congaree National Park](https://www.travelonthereg.com/things-to-do-in-congaree-national-park/) protects one of the largest intact bottomland hardwood forests in the country, with boardwalk trails through massive old-growth trees and peaceful kayaking.
